openalex-w7204763522: Solid-state batteries need electrolytes that bake at lower heat. This paper tested special titanium- and germanium-based glasses as helpers for fusing LATP ceramic grains. The team chased cooler firing and less resistance where grains meet. A battery study of baking better solid electrolytes.
arxiv-2606-16122: Many AI systems reason in words alone, but humans think with pictures too. This paper studies AI reasoning with visual grounding — connecting each step of thought to actual regions of an image. The authors explore how tying language to what the model literally sees improves its reasoning, aimed at multimodal AI researchers.
arxiv-2606-16222: Large language models "think" in a compressed internal space before producing words. Latent Thought Flow makes that hidden reasoning more efficient, letting the model work through ideas in its latent space with less compute. The paper presents the method for AI researchers trying to make chain-of-thought-style reasoning cheaper and faster.
arxiv-2606-16622: Twist-lore sheets pen leapers in dales — dip zones of dash — and dales can hum as one. This paper charts dale-to-dale hum and tang-polar lean in three-dale twist packs. For twist-lore seers who read quirk phases in skewed sheets.
arxiv-2606-16722: Physicists who test tiny magnetic sensors need a room with almost no magnetic noise — and the same quiet every time. This paper builds such a magnetic environment, stable in space and time down to the picotesla level (a trillionth of a tesla). It is an engineering paper for precision measurement labs.
arxiv-2606-16822: Should AI just answer science questions, or help students DO science? This paper frames AI as a partner in learning about, doing, and engaging with science — with 'vigilance' (staying alert to AI errors) as the key to productive use. It is for science education researchers.
